document.tekst_begin: Productiviteitsgroei stimuleren? Vier krachten in actie Leonardo Fuligni Uit het rapport ‘De staat van het mkb 2026’ komt een duidelijke boodschap naar voren: het mkb groeit structureel beperkt door, en productiviteit speelt hier een grote rol in. Het mkb is niet alleen veel minder productief dan het grootbedrijf; er bestaan vaak ook enorme verschillen binnen het mkb zelf. We hebben bijzonder innovatieve groeibedrijven die banen creëren en de economie van de toekomst vormgeven. Echter, het brede mkb ofwel ‘het peloton’ valt steeds vaker achter. De tien procent meest productieve mkb -bedrijven zijn gemiddeld 6,8 keer zo productief als de tien procent minst productieve. De cijfers laten zien dat een kleine groep koplopers het goed doet , maar dat het gemiddelde mkb-bedrijf worstelt met productiviteitsgroei. Als we willen dat onze economie wereldwijd concurrerend blijft, moeten we daarom investeren in productiviteitsgroei. Waar loopt productiviteitsgroei stroef? Vraag een gemiddelde mkb-ondernemer waar hij/ zij wakker van ligt, en productiviteit sgroei komt zelden ter sprake . Daarnaast zijn ook maatregelen uit de 2e nota van wijziging opgenomen. Op 3 november heeft het kabinet verdere wijzigingen aan het Belastingplan 2027 en omtrent box 3 aangekondigd. Het CPB heeft deze besluitvorming nog niet kunnen verwerken en verwacht de certificering hiervan niet vóór 12 november af te kunnen ronden. In totaal zijn vier fiscale maatregelen aan een uitvoerige toetsing onderworpen. Deze maatregelen hebben een beoordeling gekregen vanwege een geraamd budgettair effect van ten minste 50 mln euro, grote gedragseffecten en/of een sterk onzekere grondslag. Het CPB acht de ramingen van de budgettaire effecten van de beoordeelde maatregelen redelijk en neutraal. document.tekst_begin: 26.0001554 1 van 5 contactpersoon info@onderzoeksraad.nl Notitie datum 3 november 2026 kenmerk 26.0001554 onderzoek Overwegaanrijding Hooge Zwaluwe onderwerp Opvolging aanbevelingen Opvolging aanbevelingen: Overwegaanrijding Hooge Zwaluwe Publicatiedatum rapport: 2 december 2025 1 Over het rapport Op woensdagmiddag 28 augustus 2024 vond er een aanrijding plaats tussen een goederentrein met een overstekende vrachtwagen op de onbeveiligde overweg Zanddijk in Hooge Zwaluwe. De machinist van de goederentrein kwam hierbij om het leven en een van de andere twee collega’s op de goederentrein raakte gewond. Op deze goederenlijn reed slechts tweemaal per week een trein.1 Door de lage frequentie van het treinverkeer op dit baanvak verwachtten overweggebruikers geen trein. document.tekst_begin: Tweede Kamer der Staten-Generaal 2 Vergaderjaar 2026–2027 Vragen gesteld door de leden der Kamer 2026Z23736 Vragen van de leden Beckerman (SP) en Bushoff (PRO) aan de Minister van Binnenlandse Zaken en Koninkrijksrelaties over de berichten «Nij Begun worstelt met lange wachttijd isolatieplannen» en «Pekelders lopen vast bij aanvraag isolatiesubsidie, gemeente schiet te hulp en trekt de knip» (ingezonden 2 november 2026). Vraag 1 Erkent u dat het onacceptabel is dat bijna 4.000 Groningers nog altijd maandenlang wachten op een definitief isolatieplan, terwijl eerder dit jaar beterschap werd beloofd? document.tekst_begin: CLINGENDEAL SCENARIOKAART Uitleg Hoe gebruik je deze kaarten? De toekomst is fundamenteel onzeker. Deze kaarten zijn dan ook geen toekomstvoorspellingen, maar toekomstverkenningen. De scenario’s zijn op verschillende manieren te gebruiken. Laat je inspireren door de onderstaande suggesties, of verzin je eigen spelregels. • Analyseer de kaarten en de bijbehorende indicatoren. Is het scenario plausibel? Moeten en kunnen we ons hier beter op voorbereiden? • Bouw je eigen scenario’s. Pak drie kaarten en leg ze naast elkaar. Combineer (elementen van) de kaarten in een verhaallijn. Welke strategische dilemma’s levert dit op? • Stress-test bestaande strategieën met behulp van de kaarten. Is de strategie in deze toekomst effectief of contraproductief? Kan de strategie aangepast worden? Deze scenariokaarten zijn ontwikkeld in het kader van de Clingendael Strategische Monitor Defensie. document.tekst_begin: Kiezen zonder verliezen? De omgeving waarin de Nederlandse krijgsmacht opereert, wordt complexer en onzekerder. Verschuivende machtsverhoudingen, snelle technologische ontwikkelingen, maatschappelijke veranderingen, economische fragmentatie en veranderingen in de natuurlijke leefomgeving beïnvloeden de voorwaarden voor militair optreden. Zij brengen nieuwe dreigingen, kansen en dilemma’s met zich mee. De wereld richting 2031 laat zich niet in één ontwikkeling of dreigingsbeeld vangen. Deze Strategische Monitor Defensie brengt daarom de belangrijkste ontwikkelingen, onzekerheden en strategische afwegingen in kaart. Centraal staat welke keuzes Nederland vandaag kan maken om onder uiteenlopende omstandigheden militair handelingsvermogen te behouden. Kiezen zonder verliezen? betekent keuzes maken die de krijgsmacht ook morgen in staat stelt haar opdracht uit te voeren, ongeacht welke kaarten de toekomst op tafel legt. items.titel: Advances in Habitat Mapping Under the Habitats Directive: Cartographic Update and Ecological Implications (Extremadura, Spain)
items.samenvatting_bron: Natura 2000 habitat maps are produced under different protocols, so differences between versions may reflect methodological refinement as well as ecological change. We compared the 2005 baseline cartography of Extremadura (south-western Spain) with updates produced in 2020–2024 for six Annex I habitats (6220*, 6310, 91B0, 91E0*, 92A0 and 92D0). We assessed mapped area, subtype composition, spatial and nomenclatural correspondence and conservation status using area-weighted chi-squared tests with Crámer’s V, transition matrices and intensity analysis. Mapped area differed from 21.4% decrease (6220*) *) to a 668.2% increase (91B0), and these differences were not statistically tested. Subtype composition changed substantially for 6220* (V = 0.556) but negligibly for 6310 (V = 0.053), where most “Mixed dehesa” overlapped areas previously mapped as “Holm oak”. Of the 2005 extent, 71.4% (6220*) and 98.5–99.0% (riparian habitats) had no spatial match in the update. Coarse baseline mapping units may partly explain this but without documentation for the riparian updates, mapping precision, survey coverage, classification criteria and ecological change cannot be separated. For these habitats, attribution is therefore not possible, which makes documentation retrieval the first priority for monitoring. The framework shows where differences between successive maps can and cannot be read as ecological change, supporting Article 17 reporting.

items.titel: Native amphibians in modern European zoos
items.samenvatting_bron: Historically, zoos and aquariums have focused on displaying exotic animals. However, the biodiversity crisis has driven a paradigm shift, with modern zoos evolving into integrated conservation hubs at the nexus of species safeguarding, species recovery, and societal engagement. Despite this shift, native amphibians remain underrepresented in European zoos, largely overshadowed by non-native exotic species. The extent to which this pattern reflects institutional priorities or visitor preferences is unclear. This study assessed the value placed on native amphibian fauna by both zoological institutions and their visitors. A survey of zoos accredited by the European Association of Zoos and Aquaria (EAZA) revealed that although nearly a third of institutions house native species, these often comprise only a small fraction of their overall amphibian holdings. Additionally, zoos with a stronger focus on threatened species tend to have a greater representation of native species, irrespective of the country's native diversity or their conservation status. Native amphibians are primarily used for education and research (both ex situ and in situ), with their presence in the surveyed zoos mainly influenced by their threatened status rather than their nativeness. Our case study of visitor preferences showed a clear preference for the display and conservation of local fauna over non-native species when perceptual biases were controlled. items.titel: A precise identification method for urban garden green spaces based on U-Net for remote sensing image segmentation
items.samenvatting_bron: With the acceleration of urbanization and the upgrading of ecological city construction demands, the precise identification and dynamic monitoring of urban garden green spaces have become the core technical support for ecological environment assessment and urban planning optimization. The traditional remote sensing image green space identification methods have problems such as strong dependence on manual features, poor adaptability to complex scenes, and high leakage rate of small target green spaces. The deep learning segmentation models still have room for improvement in terms of boundary segmentation accuracy and shadow interference suppression. Therefore, this study proposes an improved U-Net model integrating three core components: a multi-scale convolution block (MSCB) for parallel multi-receptive-field feature extraction, a channel-spatial dual attention fusion module (CSAM) embedded in skip connections for interference suppression, and an adaptive weighted hybrid loss function for sample imbalance mitigation. items.titel: GOOGLE EARTH ENGINE-BASED FLOOD SUSCEPTIBILITY ANALYSIS IN THE VICINITY OF FLOOD DETENTION PONDS IN KUALA LUMPUR
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban blue-green infrastructure, such as water detention ponds, is increasingly threatened by rapid landscape transformation. While watershed-wide transitions have been extensively modelled, analysing localised human-environment interactions requires targeted spatial limits that isolate neighbourhood-scale development pressures from the broader regional context. In this regard, the Kuala Lumpur Local Plan 2040 (KLLP 2040) identifies green and blue corridors as a key planning component. It also proposes optimising lakes and flood-retention ponds as recreational parks, establishing ecological corridors, and protecting these areas' functions. This study employs a buffer-based GIS framework to examine localised land-use and land-cover (LULC) changes within 200 m of flood detention ponds from 2010 to 2025, utilising Google Earth Engine (GEE). The spatial threshold is based on urban planning and spatial analysis considerations. MCDA-AHP analysis shows that 6 ponds (25%) were classified as very high and high risk, with Kolam Takungan Banjir (KTB) Danau Kota recording the highest MCDA index (0.938). Ultimately, this neighbourhood-scale buffer approach provides a precise spatial diagnostic tool for urban planners to monitor immediate development encroachment and implement targeted stormwater mitigation policies.

items.samenvatting_bron: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to inform urban planning. Urban planning has traditionally focused on infrastructure and operational performance, with giving less attention to social inclusion, psychological well-being, and urban equity. AI adoption is often based on technological advancements without a systematic approach towards sustainable and livable cities. This leaves a critical gap in how AI can contribute to making cities more resilient, inclusive and adaptive to environmental changes. items.titel: Water-Sensitive Urban Design in Sub-Saharan African Secondary Cities: Institutional Barriers, Informality, and Pathways toward Context-Sensitive Blue-Green Infrastructure Governance
items.samenvatting_bron: Water-Sensitive Urban Design (WSUD) has, since its formulation in Australia in the early 1990s, become a widely referenced paradigm for integrating stormwater, groundwater, and water-supply management into urban planning. Its fullest articulation, the water-sensitive city, describes a societal transition rather than a design technique alone. Its diffusion across the Global South has, however, exposed a translation problem: frameworks developed for well-resourced, formally planned cities do not travel cleanly into the institutional, fiscal, and tenurial conditions of many Sub-Saharan African secondary cities. The region also lacks a single shared vocabulary: South Africa has a formal WSUD framework, while Kenya, Uganda, and Rwanda organise comparable interventions as nature-based solutions. This narrative review draws on 24 sources identified through a documented search and selection procedure. It synthesises the conceptual evolution of WSUD and examines four recurring barriers to its translation: legal and regulatory fragmentation; fiscal constraint at municipal level; the mismatch between formal design frameworks and informally held land; and colonial and postcolonial drainage legacies. items.samenvatting_bron: Municipalities increasingly govern climate change through several planning instruments rather than a single comprehensive plan. Yet successive plans are often read as a linear progression, obscuring the persistence, changing functions, and overlap of sectoral priorities. items.titel: Green for whom? Sociospatial inequalities in public green space accessibility in the context of a Latin American city
items.samenvatting_bron: Public green spaces are essential for urban well-being, social inclusion, and environmental sustainability. However, access to these spaces is often unevenly distributed, particularly in large, consolidated cities. This study examines environmental justice in access to public green spaces in the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area, México, one of the largest urban regions in Latin America. Using a mixed methods approach, we combined Geographic Information Systems (GIS), socioeconomic indicators and social perception surveys to evaluate the distribution, accessibility, and use of public green space across different levels of socioeconomic marginalization. Accessibility was measured using pedestrian network distances of 300 m and 500 m. Results showed strong spatial inequalities. Only 23% of the population lives within 300 m of a public green space and 49% within 500 m. Areas with very low and low marginalization account for 55% of the metropolitan population but represent nearly 70% of residents with access within 300 m. In contrast, populations living in highly marginalized areas remain strongly underrepresented even when the accessibility threshold increases to 500 m. Green space availability per capita also differed significantly among municipalities and marginalization levels, with the lowest values concentrated in highly marginalized neighborhoods. items.titel: From cooling potential to marginal benefits: A smart-city framework for equitable green infrastructure planning under extreme heat
items.samenvatting_bron: Extreme heat is among the most consequential climate-related hazards in cities. In this Viewpoint, we propose the Marginal Health Benefit (MBₗ) framework as a conceptual basis for the future empirical application and testing of urban greening strategies in climate-resilient smart cities. The framework integrates GeoAI, fine-scale thermal modelling and socio-demographic vulnerability data to shift planning attention from aggregate canopy cover and cooling performance towards the distribution of health benefits among vulnerable populations. It evaluates green infrastructure according to its expected capacity to reduce the probability of heat-related illness or mortality for specific populations in specific locations. We argue that recent advances in GeoAI, open satellite data, building-footprint datasets, and fine-scale urban modelling make this approach increasingly feasible at neighbourhood scale, including in data-sparse cities. Rather than maximising canopy provision or cooling performance in isolation, urban heat resilience should prioritise interventions where vulnerability is greatest and additional greening is expected to achieve the greatest reduction in heat-related harm. This reframing could help spatial planners and public administrators direct limited greening investment towards locations expected to provide the greatest marginal health benefit.

items.titel: ECOSYSTEM SERVICES AS COMPARABLE ELEMENTS: EXAMINING THE POTENTIAL FOR NATURE INCLUSIVITY IN PROPERTY VALUATION
items.samenvatting_bron: Ecosystem services motivate growing interest in nature-related comparable elements in property valuation, but their application requires clearly defined indicators and market evidence. This study examines vegetation greenness and advertised nightly hotel tariffs in Bogor, Indonesia, using 106 room-rate observations from 94 hotel groups collected in August 2025. Separate hedonic regressions include mean normalised difference vegetation index (NDVI) within 50, 100, 250 and 500 m buffers and 12 locational and accommodation controls. Inference uses hotel-clustered standard errors and Holm adjustment for multiple testing. NDVI coefficients are positive across all radii, with associations at 100–500 m remaining significant at 5% after adjustment. Spatial models provide exploratory support for this pattern. The findings suggest that environmental indicators associated with ecosystem services may inform accommodation price analysis and comparable market research, subject to broader validation before application in valuation guidance.

items.titel: How roads impact wildlife in the world’s greenest country
items.samenvatting_bron: Roads provide important social benefits but also cause wildlife mortality through vehicle collisions. To address the lack of systematic data in emerging economies, we monitored wildlife roadkill on three major roads in Suriname: Paramaribo–Albina (145 km), Paramaribo–Atjoni (185 km), and Paramaribo–South Drain (252 km). Surveys were conducted monthly over 12 months, totaling 13,392 km of vehicle monitoring and 576 km on-foot. We recorded 1,553 carcasses representing 151 species, including four globally threatened species. Reptiles were the most affected group, followed by birds, mammals, and amphibians. The most frequently recorded species were Didelphis marsupialis , Helicops angulatus , Erythrolamprus cobella , Eunectes murinus, and Tyto alba . Roadkill hotspots were concentrated along the Paramaribo–Albina Road. Forest cover within road buffers declined between 1985 and 2023, indicating ongoing landscape transformation. We recommend wildlife crossings, exclusion fencing, and applying the mitigation hierarchy to future infrastructure projects to balance development and biodiversity conservation in Suriname.

It demonstrates how ecological degradation and microbial disruption reshape environmental exposure pathways across urban, agricultural, and aquatic systems, thereby intensifying disease risk, toxic burden, and health inequities. This chapter further analyzes how land-use decisions, infrastructure design, and governance choices modulate microbial and ecological functions, thereby amplifying vulnerability or strengthening resilience. Emerging technologies—including molecular surveillance, environmental DNA analysis, biosensing platforms, and digital monitoring networks—are critically examined for their capacity to translate biological insight into adaptive sustainability interventions. items.titel: Challenges and Opportunities for FAIR Marine eDNA Data Publication Workflows
items.samenvatting_bron: Marine environmental DNA (eDNA) approaches are increasingly integrated into biodiversity monitoring, generating interconnected data products spanning sample collection, laboratory processing, bioinformatics and derived biodiversity observations. No single repository accommodates every component of an eDNA study. Sequence data are generally deposited in molecular archives such as the Sequence Read Archive (SRA) or the European Nucletide Archive (ENA), derived occurrence records in biodiversity repositories such as the Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS) or Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF), and supplementary files in institutional or general-purpose repositories. Publishing a complete study can therefore require submissions to several platforms and creation of reliable links between the resulting records (Takahashi et al. 2025). Standards and tools support different stages of eDNA data publication, and users need to connect multiple independent and not interoperable digital tools in order to complete a full FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) eDNA dataset publication. The availability of individual technical components does not ensure that publication is practical, efficient or aligned with user needs (Rajbhandari et al. 2025). We surveyed eDNA practitioners to assess current practices, barriers, priorities and support requirements to identify gaps and build a suite of tools to meet the needs of users. items.titel: Environmental DNA metabarcoding in ecological status assessment: Agreement and bias relative to traditional fish‐based evaluations
items.samenvatting_bron: Freshwater ecosystems are experiencing unprecedented degradation worldwide. Regulatory frameworks such as the Water Framework Directive mandate standardized biological monitoring to assess ecological status against legally binding thresholds and guide restoration action. Although environmental DNA metabarcoding offers an efficient, non‐invasive monitoring tool, whether water‐sample eDNA can deliver reliable fish‐based ecological status assessment, especially for WFD threshold decisions, remains insufficiently validated. We conducted eDNA metabarcoding and electrofishing surveys at 50 wadeable stream sites spanning four hydro‐geomorphological river types in the Balaton catchment, Hungary. items.samenvatting_bron: The Chinese Bahaba ( Bahaba taipingensis , Sciaenidae) is a Critically Endangered, Grade I state-protected marine fish in China. Reliable, non-invasive monitoring tools are urgently needed to assess wild populations and evaluate ongoing restocking efforts. In this study, we developed and validated three species-specific TaqMan qPCR assays targeting mitochondrial 12S rRNA, ND5, and D-loop loci for B. taipingensis . Primer–probe sets were evaluated in silico against GenBank databases and in vitro using tissue DNA from B. taipingensis and sympatric sciaenids, alongside positive eDNA samples; assay sensitivity was quantified using synthetic target DNA standards. All three assays exhibited high specificity and robust amplification, with the 12S rRNA assay (Bhb_12S) demonstrating superior low-copy sensitivity and minimal non-specific products. items.titel: Smart City Initiatives and Prospects for Climate-Resilient Urban Food Systems in South Africa: A Systematic Review
items.samenvatting_bron: Climate change significantly drives South African food systems into disarray. This article contributes to discussions on strategies towards ensuring that cities can absorb climate shocks while maintaining equitable access to nutrition. Underpinned by the Urban Food System Strategy and Resilience Approach and drawing on a systematic literature review of 85 texts identified in Scopus and the Web of Science, this article explores how smart cities can be harnessed for climate-resilient food systems and identifies the challenges of leveraging smart cities for food system transformation in South Africa. The review reveals that building climate resilience into food systems within South African smart cities requires a shift from traditional, linear supply chains to circular, tech-enabled urban ecosystems. This involves investments in digital infrastructure and precision urbanism, the implementation of nature-based solutions, the adoption of decentralised and shortened value chains, and investments in socio-economic resilience and equity. Future research should focus on integrating technology with social inclusion, circularity, and localised production to address rising food insecurity.

items.titel: Interdisciplinary Pathways to Climate-Resilient Landscapes
items.samenvatting_bron: Climate change, land-use dynamics, and ecosystem resilience are deeply intertwined challenges that shape biodiversity outcomes, ecosystem services (ESs), and human well-being across rural, peri-urban, and urban landscapes. This chapter advances an interdisciplinary framework for understanding how climate drivers and environmental stressors interact with land-use change, agricultural intensification, and urbanization to influence ecosystem vulnerability and adaptive capacity. By integrating climate science, land-use and land-cover change research, biodiversity and ESs theory, agriculture and urban studies, and governance perspectives, this chapter moves beyond sectoral analyses to reveal systemic feedbacks, thresholds, and trade-offs that constrain or enable resilience. It critically examines how land-use decisions drive ecosystem degradation, biodiversity loss, and climate amplification, while highlighting opportunities for climate-smart agriculture, multifunctional landscapes, and nature-based solutions. items.titel: Zeker 36 ontheffingen voor afsteken vuurwerk verleend
items.samenvatting_bron: Een maand voor de jaarwisseling hebben gemeenten zeker 36 ontheffingen voor het afsteken van vuurwerk afgegeven. Dat blijkt uit een rondgang van het ANP. Niet alle gemeenten reageerden op vragen van het persbureau. Het werkelijke aantal ontheffingen kan dus hoger zijn. Dat geldt ook voor het aantal ontheffingen dat is aangevraagd. Dat zijn er volgens het ANP zeker 80. Bijna alle gemeenten die ontheffingen afgaven, liggen in het noorden of oosten van het land. Drie gemeenten springen eruit: de Drentse gemeente Borger-Odoorn en de Friese gemeenten Noardeast-Fryslân en Opsterland. Samen gaven ze veertien vergunningen af. Landelijk verbod Vanaf dit jaar geldt voor het afsteken van consumentenvuurwerk een landelijk verbod . Onder voorwaarden mogen gemeenten ontheffingen verlenen. Zo moeten aanvragers een vereniging of stichting zijn die bij de Kamer van Koophandel staat ingeschreven. Ook moeten ze een duidelijke band hebben met de gemeente waar ze vuurwerk willen afsteken. Verder moet er een veiligheidsplan zijn en moeten twee getrainde supervisors toezicht houden. Eerder deze maand bleek uit een rondgang van de NOS dat zeker driekwart van de gemeenten geen enkele ontheffing zal afgeven. Volgens de Vereniging van Nederlandse Gemeenten was voor een aantal gemeenten de voorbereidingstijd tekort.

items.titel: Meer ruimte voor dronevliegers, regels rond vijf luchthavens versoepeld
items.samenvatting_bron: Hobbyisten en professionele dronevliegers mogen sinds gisteren op veel meer plekken in Nederland hun drone de lucht in sturen. Dat komt door een versoepeling van de regels voor het vliegen rond vijf niet-militaire luchthavens. Door de invoering van de nieuwe regels mogen dronevliegers nu in grote delen van Amsterdam, Rotterdam en Groningen vliegen, waar dat voorheen voor hobbyisten verboden was. Ook rond Lelystad en Maastricht zijn de regels verruimd. Tot nu toe was het verboden om zonder toestemming van de luchtverkeersleiding in een straal van zo'n 15 kilometer rond luchthavens drones te laten vliegen, maar het ministerie van Infrastructuur en Waterstaat (I&W) heeft samen met Luchtverkeersleiding Nederland (LVNL) deze gebieden opnieuw ingedeeld. Op veel plekken mag nu op minimaal vijf kilometer van een luchthaven zonder toestemming worden gevlogen tot een hoogte van 120 meter. Op die afstand vliegen opstijgende en landende vliegtuigen volgens het ministerie van I&W hoog genoeg om veilig drones toe te laten. Voor infrastructuur, politie of brandweer Drones worden steeds vaker ingezet, bijvoorbeeld voor de inspectie van dijken en andere infrastructuur, en voor andere maatschappelijke taken van onder meer politie en brandweer . Daardoor neemt de vraag naar ruimte in het luchtruim toe, zegt de LVNL. De versoepeling van de regels moet ook de werkdruk bij de luchtverkeersleiding verminderen.
